Hi Ben,

We're seeing a sharp degradation on our production traffic starting ~13:55 PDT after the new model variant (v2028-06-07-v2) started receiving canary traffic. Symptoms: sustained 5xx rate (~1.8%), p95 jumped from ~220ms to ~1.9s, p99 to ~4.8s, and overall throughput dropped as clients started timing out. This is affecting our ingestion workers and one of our downstream jobs missed an SLA.

I attached a small tar with sample request IDs and corresponding logs. A few request ids: req_3f4a, req_3f88, req_40b2 — you'll see long kernel waits and occasional 502 from the Redwood endpoint.

We didn't change client side, so this coincided exactly with the canary ring. Can you triage urgently? We have an internal compliance window tomorrow and need a mitigation plan or rollback asap.

Thanks,
Sarah

Acknowledged — opening P1 incident INC-20280608-57 now. Initial triage notes below (quick, preliminary):

What I see so far: canary traffic for v2028-06-07-v2 started ~13:50 PDT. Host-level metrics show a 30-40% increase in kernel scheduling stalls for the variant fleet in us-west-2 and elevated GPU device utilization variance (short, frequent spikes). Runtime traces show longer KV cache misses and increased time spent in quantized kernel fallback paths for longer sequences (>1024 tokens).

Immediate mitigation I'm actioning now: 
- Rolling traffic for generate-text back to previous stable variant (v2028-05-20-v1) for Zephyr's account only (canary rollback targeted).
- Temporarily increase concurrency limit for their dedicated shared pool and add a short autoscale burst for the region.
- Collecting more request ids and traces; attaching early notes.

Please standby while I confirm rollbacks complete. If rollback fails or latency persists, we'll route their requests to a cold standby region and open a broader rollback.

Update: rollback targeted for Zephyr completed at 15:57 PDT. Post-rollback metrics (first 6 minutes): p95 ~240ms, p99 ~420ms, 5xx rate down to 0.12%. Throughput returned to expected baseline. I attached a screenshot of the verification dashboard.

Preliminary root cause (pre-RCA): a config change in the variant's runtime build enabled an aggressive KV expiry heuristic intended to reduce memory retention for short sequences. For mixed-length workloads Zephyr sends, this caused excessive KV churn and higher cache miss penalties. Additionally, for a subset of long sequences the new variant exercised a quantized kernel path that had a conservative fallback to a slower FP path under certain alignment conditions — this exacerbated tail latency.

Next steps:
- Full RCA and repro harness by EOD tomorrow (owner: infra-testing team, lead Hannah).
- Create a canary-safeguard checklist (owner: SRE, Soojin) covering cache heuristics, quant kernel test vectors, and per-account canary ramps.
- Customer follow-up & credit assessment (owner: Marissa).

Soojin
SRE — Inference Platform
Redwood Inference
